name: Glean
summary: Glean builds enterprise search and agent software. Its June 2025 financing valued the company at $7.2 billion.
overview: Glean connects enterprise knowledge across applications and uses that context to power search and AI agents for employees.

facts.label: Latest disclosed financing
facts.note: Reuters reported the company's third capital raise in less than two years.

bull_case: A trusted enterprise context layer can become the distribution point for search, knowledge management and agent workflows across a company's software stack.
bear_case: Large platform vendors control core productivity surfaces, and premium valuation multiples require Glean to prove durable growth and retention beyond a narrow search use case.
directory_notes: Watch agent adoption, retention and platform competition.

intelligence.description: Enterprise search and AI-agent platform that connects information across workplace applications.
company: Glean indexes enterprise information across the applications employees already use and applies that context to search and AI-agent experiences. Its core challenge is turning broad integrations into a trusted, high-frequency employee workflow.
Reuters reported that Glean's June 2025 funding round valued the company at $7.2 billion, following rapid valuation growth from $2.2 billion in early 2024.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Glean is a high-value test of whether enterprise AI can monetize through a horizontal knowledge layer rather than a single application. Its progress also informs the competitive balance between standalone AI platforms and incumbent productivity suites.

changed.text: Glean raised new capital at a reported $7.2B valuation.

takeaways: Enterprise context and trust are the product's key assets.
The valuation assumes AI agents become a durable enterprise workflow.
Microsoft, Google and other suite vendors are material competitive risks.
